sol.title: Sol
sol.definition: A Sol is one day on Mars. It is a little longer than a day on Earth: about 24 hours and 39 minutes.
sol.nasa_fact: Teams that drive NASA rovers sometimes change their work hours to match Mars time.

moxie.title: MOXIE
moxie.definition: MOXIE is a small oxygen factory. It takes air from Mars, which is mostly carbon dioxide, and splits out the oxygen so people can breathe.
moxie.nasa_fact: MOXIE traveled on the Perseverance rover and made about 122 grams of oxygen on Mars.

electrolisis_co2.title: Splitting CO₂
electrolisis_co2.definition: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is the gas we breathe out. Using electricity, you can break it apart into oxygen and carbon monoxide.
electrolisis_co2.nasa_fact: MOXIE does this at a super hot 800 °C to get oxygen from the air of Mars.

crater_jezero.title: Jezero Crater
crater_jezero.definition: A huge bowl in the ground on Mars. Billions of years ago it was a lake with a river delta.
crater_jezero.nasa_fact: The Perseverance rover landed here in February 2021 to look for signs of ancient life.

crater_gale.title: Gale Crater
crater_gale.definition: A crater on Mars with a tall mountain in the middle, called Mount Sharp. The mountain is made of layers of rock.
crater_gale.nasa_fact: The Curiosity rover landed in Gale Crater in 2012 and found clay that formed with water.

regolito.title: Regolith
regolito.definition: Regolith is the loose dust and tiny pieces of rock that cover the ground on Mars.
regolito.nasa_fact: Mars regolith has a salt in it called perchlorate that is bad for people, so astronauts would need to clean it first.

cme.title: Coronal Mass Ejection (CME)
cme.definition: A giant cloud of tiny particles that the Sun throws into space. If it hits a planet, it can damage machines and bother people.
cme.nasa_fact: NASA's DONKI system keeps track of these clouds and warns when one is heading toward a planet.

fulguracion_solar.title: Solar Flare
fulguracion_solar.definition: A giant burst of light and energy from the Sun. Flares have letters: A, B, C, M and X. X is the strongest.
fulguracion_solar.nasa_fact: Big M and X flares can cause radio blackouts and dangerous radiation for astronauts.

probioticos.title: Probiotics
probioticos.definition: Probiotics are good bacteria that live in your tummy and help keep you healthy.
probioticos.nasa_fact: A NASA study found that a probiotic called Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG helps the gut cope with space radiation.

radiacion_cosmica.title: Space Radiation
radiacion_cosmica.definition: Tiny, super-fast particles that come from the Sun and from far-away stars. On Mars, nothing like Earth's magnetic shield protects you from them.
radiacion_cosmica.nasa_fact: A tool on the Curiosity rover called RAD measures radiation on Mars so we know how to protect astronauts.

osdr.title: OSDR
osdr.definition: OSDR is NASA's free online library of results from science experiments done in space.
osdr.nasa_fact: Anyone can read it. Studies about astronauts' tummies and brains come from this data.

perseverance.title: Perseverance
perseverance.definition: A car-sized NASA robot that explores Mars. It collects rock samples to bring to Earth someday.
perseverance.nasa_fact: It landed in Jezero Crater in 2021 and carries the MOXIE machine.

opportunity.title: Opportunity
opportunity.definition: A NASA robot that landed on Mars in 2004. It was only supposed to work for 90 Sols.
opportunity.nasa_fact: It worked for almost 14 years, until a giant dust storm in 2018 covered its solar panels.

tormenta_polvo.title: Dust Storm
tormenta_polvo.definition: Wind that lifts up dust on Mars. It can cover solar panels and block sunlight for days or weeks.
tormenta_polvo.nasa_fact: Some Martian dust storms grow big enough to cover the whole planet.

sismometro_seis.title: SEIS Seismometer
sismometro_seis.definition: A super-sensitive tool that feels the shaking of the ground on Mars. It is like a stethoscope for a planet.
sismometro_seis.nasa_fact: SEIS flew on the InSight lander and recorded more than 1,300 Marsquakes.

insight.title: InSight
insight.definition: A NASA lander that stayed in one spot on Mars to listen to what is inside the planet.
insight.nasa_fact: It landed in 2018 and finished its mission in December 2022.

martemoto.title: Marsquake
martemoto.definition: An earthquake on Mars. It happens when the rocky crust of the planet cracks or moves.
martemoto.nasa_fact: Thanks to Marsquakes, InSight could measure how thick Mars's crust is and how big its core is.

minutos_luz.title: Light-minutes
minutos_luz.definition: The time it takes a radio signal to travel from one place to another. Between Earth and Mars it takes 3 to 22 minutes, depending on where each planet is.
minutos_luz.nasa_fact: Because of this delay, you cannot chat live with Mars. Every question and answer takes a long time.
